requirement: The EPA determined that the WDA facility is a single source for the purposes of applying the PSD, NNSR, and Title V permit programs.
source: EPA source determination analysis memo-to-file dated June 26, 2019

requirement: For the purposes of determining the potential emissions, the EPA has determined it is appropriate to use the center of the WDA as the point to estimate vessel emissions within 25 miles of the OCS source comprising the WDA.
source: EPA source determination analysis memo-to-file dated June 26, 2019

requirement: Similarly, emissions from offshore export cable-laying activities will be calculated separately using the center of those activities because it is a separate source.
source: EPA source determination analysis memo-to-file dated June 26, 2019

requirement: A vessel will not be considered an OCS source if it temporarily attaches itself to the seabed due to a safety issue, engine failure, or a storm at sea, as the vessel is not considered to be erected on the seabed for the purposes of exploring, developing, or producing resources therefrom.
scope: Vessels temporarily attached to the seabed

requirement: The criteria 'erected thereon' is met when a service fleet vessel attaches itself to the seabed and becomes stationary, and is used thereafter for the purpose of exploring, developing, or producing resources from the seabed like constructing a wind turbine generator (WTG) or electric service platform (ESP).
scope: Service fleet vessels attached to the seabed

requirement: The collection of WTGs and the ESP constitute a 'facility,' as that term is used in the definition of 'OCS source' in 40 C.F.R. § 55.2, and as a 'major stationary source' as that term is used in the PSD, NNSR, and Title V permitting programs.
scope: Wind turbine generators and electric service platform

requirement: The emission units on the service fleet vessel are still subject to the permit's NNSR offset requirements once the service fleet vessel is no longer meeting the criteria for an OCS source.
scope: Service fleet vessels no longer meeting OCS source criteria

requirement: NOx is a measured pollutant for the criteria pollutant NO2 and a precursor for ozone and PM2.5.
VOC is a measured pollutant and precursor for the criteria pollutant ozone.
Based on PM10 emissions being greater than 25 tpy, the EPA has determined the WDA Facility is significant for PM emissions.
SO2 is a criteria pollutant and a precursor for the criteria pollutant PM2.5.

The WDA facility's potential emissions include emissions from helicopters which are not required to be part of the potential to emit calculation for the WDA facility. Helicopter emissions are de minimis for the WDA facility, and whether their emissions are included or not will have no impact on determining PSD applicability.
PM 2.5 annual and 24-hr impacts must be below 0.05 μg/m3 and 0.27 μg/m3 respectively at Class I PSD areas
PM 10 annual and 24-hr impacts must be below 0.2 μg/m3 and 0.3 μg/m3 respectively
NO2 annual impacts must be below 0.1 μg/m3
source: 61 FR 38250, "Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD) and Nonattainment New Source Review (NSR)"

requirement: Assess air quality impacts and impairment to visibility, soils, and vegetation due to operational period emissions of the WDA facility and general commercial, residential, industrial and other growth associated with the operational period of the WDA facility.
The results of both visibility analyses provided results well below screening thresholds.

Vineyard Wind provided conservative assessments of impacts on vegetation based on maximum operational period air quality impacts in any location, even if the impacts occurred over water (i.e., where there is no terrestrial vegetation).
The WDA facility's potential emissions of NOx and VOC are above 50 tpy, the threshold for NNSR, during the construction phase.

Only NOx emissions continue to be above 50 tpy during the operational phase, but both NOx and VOC emissions continue to be subject to NNSR permitting since the potential emissions of the WDA facility exceeded the NNSR thresholds for at least one year.
OECLA's emissions in any one year only exceed the NNSR threshold for NOx emissions during the construction phase.

Emissions during the construction phase for the WDA facility and OECLA will end when construction and commissioning (for the WDA facility) is completed and thus these emissions are considered 'one-time' emissions, meaning they will not continue out into the future.
All engines at the WTGs and ESP to meet the standards for marine engines in 40 C.F.R. 1042
scope: Engines on Offshore Wind Turbine Generators (WTGs) and Electrical Service Platform (ESP)

requirement: All engines on most vessels when those vessels are operating within the definition of an OCS source to meet the standards for marine engines in either 40 C.F.R. part 94 or part 1042
scope: Engines on vessels operating as an Outer Continental Shelf (OCS) source

requirement: Foreign flagged vessels are exempt from having to meet the marine standards within 40 C.F.R. parts 94 and 1042 and instead are required to meet the emission standards in 40 C.F.R. § 1043
scope: Foreign flagged vessels operating as an OCS source

requirement: Certain foreign flagged vessels are required to meet the emission standards for Tier 2 engines in 40 C.F.R. § 94.8 due to LAER requirements
scope: Certain foreign flagged vessels operating as an OCS source

requirement: All internal combustion engines located on a vessel, while the vessel meets the definition of an OCS, or located on WTGs and an ESP that meet the definition of an OCS source, are subject to 40 C.F.R. part 63, subpart ZZZZ (National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants)
scope: Internal combustion engines on vessels and on WTGs/ESP that meet the definition of an OCS source
